{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABVv18MQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6Pzg_R_XU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 26, "title": "Implement PMX SDEF skinning in TSL with local YYB Miku model verification", "body": "## Problem

PMX SDEF vertices currently render as BDEF2. Implement actual SDEF skinning for Three.js r186 TSL / NodeMaterial on both WebGPU and WebGL2, so a real SDEF-containing PMX model deforms correctly.

The separate parser API correction is tracked by [mmd-parser#23](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-parser/issues/23). **Do not start the dependent runtime implementation against the old parser behavior or silently use a vendored parser.** The parser change must be published to npm and the dependency updated before final integration, or this Issue should remain open until that prerequisite exists.

## Real-model validation target

Use **YYB式初音ミク 10th v1.02** as the first manually obtained, real MMD SDEF model:

- Original distribution page: https://bowlroll.net/file/146083
- The babylon-mmd SDEF documentation uses this model for an SDEF-enabled vs. disabled comparison.
- Download only from the author's distribution according to its terms. Verify the README/license locally.
- **Local-only by default:** model files, textures, archive, and motion data must stay under a Git-ignored private asset directory such as `examples/assets/private/yyb-miku-10th/`; never commit, upload as CI artifacts, publish to GitHub Pages, or include in an npm tarball.
- Do **not** change the existing published MMD examples, their current PMD/VMD/VPD assets, asset manifest, screenshots, or GitHub Pages example catalog as part of this Issue.
- A future replacement of the public example model is a **separate decision and Issue**, contingent on reviewing the model's actual license/README and whether redistribution/hosted display is authorized. Do not assume permission.

## Implementation scope

- Consume the released `mmd-parser` version that distinguishes SDEF (`type: 3`) and correctly converts `C/R0/R1`; update package/lockfile and document the minimum required parser version.
- Preserve SDEF vertex data through GeometryBuilder as attributes, alongside existing skinIndex/skinWeight and BDEF vertices in mixed meshes.
- Implement the reference SDEF deformation (with correct input-space conventions, two bone matrices, C/R0/R1, weighted rotation, and normals) as TSL, not a separate GLSL-only path.
- Maintain standard BDEF behavior and the existing morph-before-skinning order. Ensure vertex morph + SDEF is covered.
- Apply identical SDEF deformation to MMDToonMaterial surface and MMDOutlineEffect, including normals, to prevent surface/outline mismatch.
- Integrate using Three.js r186 node lifecycle and bone transform update behavior. Consider bind matrices, morphs, normals and outline/shadow behavior. Do not bypass or double-apply standard skinning.
- If a technical limitation is encountered, record and resolve it in the PR instead of treating BDEF2 fallback as passing SDEF support.

## Local real-model viewing (not a merge gate)

Provide a **local-only** workflow to load the privately obtained YYB PMX and its textures into the actual MMDLoader and inspect deformation. Include an SDEF vertex count and simple controls for a meaningful bend/pose, and preferably an optional SDEF vs. BDEF2 comparison on the same model. Allow use of actual compatible motion if available without bundling it.

Implement the viewer/tooling in a way that cannot be copied into `dist/examples` or deployed by the current public Pages build. For example, use a separate Git-ignored local viewer entry or a local-only route guarded by the development server, rather than adding a public `examples/*.html` page (the build copies HTML there).

If the real model needs manual download, document exact local placement and startup instructions; do not add any agent/CI requirement to authenticate to BowlRoll or retrieve a third-party licensed archive.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Declares and resolves an npm-published `mmd-parser` version supporting SDEF `type: 3` and right-handed C/R0/R1; never uses unpublished local or vendored parser.
- [ ] GeometryBuilder correctly distinguishes mixed BDEF/SDEF vertices and retains SDEF C/R0/R1 and skinning type in suitable vertex attributes.
- [ ] SDEF deformation follows an explicitly documented reference algorithm; CPU reference tests cover rest pose, one-bone weights, two-bone rotation, mixed vertex types and coordinate conversion.
- [ ] The TSL implementation is actually exercised on mandatory WebGL2 via WebGPURenderer(`{forceWebGL:true}`), and on native WebGPU when available; checks compare against an independent CPU reference (not only against a screenshot with self-generated expectations).
- [ ] Normal transformation, standard vertex morph + SDEF and mixed BDEF/SDEF models are tested.
- [ ] Toon surface, outline, and any shared geometry deformation remain aligned under SDEF.
- [ ] The existing PMD, BDEF1, BDEF2, BDEF4, morph, material, outline and animation regression tests continue passing.
- [ ] Real-model local viewer instructions are complete, use actual MMDLoader with YYB PMX, provide at least one way to move the model's bones, and report SDEF vertex count. This workflow may be manually exercised by the maintainer; no manual visual check is a pre-merge requirement.
- [ ] The local viewer cannot be accidentally deployed via `npm run build:examples` or the GitHub Pages workflow, and is not included in `npm pack`.
- [ ] Existing public examples/assets, screenshots, static-site manifest, and example URLs remain unchanged.
- [ ] No YYB model, textures, archive, redistribution-only license material, or newly acquired copyrighted assets are committed, uploaded to CI, or served publicly.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run build:examples`, `npm run test:examples`, and isolated `npm pack` consumer tests pass.
- [ ] No manual download, account login, visual inspection, or post-merge deployment result is required to approve/complete the PR.

## Required post-merge verification

**None** for Issue/PR completion.

After merge the maintainer may locally open the real YYB model, bend the joints, and visually compare SDEF and BDEF2. This manual check is informative, not a GitWeave blocker. Public example replacement requires a later license and technical review and is **out of scope**.
